title: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

relationships.phenotype: INTELLECTUAL DEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH POOR GROWTH AND WITH OR WITHOUT SEIZURES OR ATAXIA

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ABCA2 gene.

checks.claim: Intellectual developmental disorder with poor growth and with or without seizures or ataxia (IDPOGSA) is caused by homozygous mutation in the ABCA2 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper links homozygous truncating ABCA2 variants to global developmental delay and intellectual disability. It does not use the IDPOGSA name and does not mention poor growth, seizures or ataxia.

paragraphs.text: IDPOGSA is an autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder. Maddirevula et al. (2019) described global developmental delay and intellectual disability in affected individuals. Aslam and Naz (2019) described cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria in affected sibs, with no brain abnormalities on MRI and with elevated low density lipoprotein levels in blood.

checks.claim: IDPOGSA is an autosomal recessive neurodevelopmental disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: Recessive inheritance is implied because homozygous variants segregated with the disorder, which fits the paper's autozygome framework. The paper does not explicitly call the ABCA2 disorder autosomal recessive.

checks.claim: Individuals affected by IDPOGSA had global developmental delay.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Individuals affected by IDPOGSA had intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: Sibs affected by IDPOGSA had cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: Symptoms of the two affected subjects were consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Sibs affected by IDPOGSA had no brain abnormalities on MRI.
checks.evidence_quote: Magnetic resonance imaging did not reveal brain abnormalities.
checks.explanation: MRI was done only on the older sib, but it is consistent with the claim.

checks.claim: Sibs affected by IDPOGSA had elevated low density lipoprotein levels in blood.
checks.evidence_quote: The levels of low density lipid proteins were elevated in blood samples of both affected individuals.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Maddirevula et al. (2019) reported 2 families in which global developmental delay and intellectual disability segregated with homozygous truncating ABCA2 variants. The index patient in 1 family (16DG0071) showed no apparent gross dysmorphism. The authors considered this phenotype different enough from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis reported by Steinberg et al. that it might be a distinct allelic disorder.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) reported 2 families in which global developmental delay and intellectual disability segregated with homozygous truncating ABCA2 variants.
checks.evidence_quote: These include two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: The index patient in family 16DG0071 with an ABCA2 variant showed no apparent gross dysmorphism.
checks.evidence_quote: Facial pictures of index (16DG0071) subject with ABCA2 showing apparent lack of gross dysmorphism.
checks.explanation: The Figure 2 legend states this.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) considered the ABCA2-related developmental delay/intellectual disability phenotype different enough from the amyotrophic lateral sclerosis reported by Steinberg et al. that it might be a distinct allelic disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: In class 3, the phenotypes observed are sufficiently different from those previously reported that we argue these may represent distinct allelic disorders
checks.explanation: ABCA2 is listed in class 3, and the paper says its phenotype is distinct from the ALS reported by Steinberg et al.

paragraphs.text: Aslam and Naz (2019) studied a consanguineous Pakistani family with 2 affected sibs. Both had symptoms consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria. Magnetic resonance imaging of the older sib showed no brain abnormalities. Both affected individuals had elevated blood levels of low density lipoproteins. The authors noted that the phenotype closely matched that of Abca2 knockout mice.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) studied a consanguineous Pakistani family with 2 sibs affected by IDPOGSA.
checks.evidence_quote: The study was conducted to identify the molecular basis of a movement disorder in a consanguineous Pakistani family.
checks.explanation: The family and the 2 affected sibs match. The paper describes the disorder as ataxia with dysarthria and does not use the term IDPOGSA.

checks.claim: Both affected sibs in the Pakistani family studied by Aslam and Naz (2019) had symptoms consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: Symptoms of the two affected subjects were consistent with cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: MRI of the older affected sib in the Pakistani family studied by Aslam and Naz (2019) showed no brain abnormalities.
checks.evidence_quote: We performed clinical assessments and magnetic resonance imaging of the older of two siblings affected with a movement disorder.
checks.explanation: The abstract also states that MRI did not reveal brain abnormalities.

checks.claim: Both affected sibs in the Pakistani family studied by Aslam and Naz (2019) had elevated blood levels of low density lipoproteins.
checks.evidence_quote: The levels of low density lipid proteins were elevated in blood samples of both affected individuals.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) noted that the phenotype of the affected Pakistani sibs closely matched that of Abca2 knockout mice.
checks.evidence_quote: The phenotype observed in our patients shows high concordance with that observed in Abca2 knockout mice.
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Maddirevula et al. (2019) found that homozygous ABCA2 variants fully segregated with the disorder in 2 families, consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) found that homozygous ABCA2 variants fully segregated with the disorder in 2 families.
checks.evidence_quote: two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

checks.claim: The segregation of homozygous ABCA2 variants in 2 families is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance of IDPOGSA.
checks.evidence_quote: two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: Full segregation of homozygous variants directly implies recessive inheritance, which fits the paper's autozygome-based recessive framework.

paragraphs.text: Maddirevula et al. (2019) used autozygome and exome analysis to study 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability. They identified a different homozygous truncating mutation in the ABCA2 gene in each family: c.740dupT (Gly248ArgfsTer38) and c.1027C-T (Gln343Ter). In both families, the mutation fully segregated with the disorder.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) used autozygome and exome analysis to study 2 families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: Autozygome and exome analysis of patients with suspected Mendelian phenotypes.
checks.explanation: This is the study method, applied to all cases, including the two ABCA2 families.

checks.claim: Maddirevula et al. (2019) identified a different homozygous truncating ABCA2 mutation in each of 2 families with developmental delay and intellectual disability.
checks.evidence_quote: fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38]) and (NM_212533.2:c.1027C>T:p.[Gln343*])
checks.explanation: The paper reports two different truncating variants in the two families.

checks.claim: One family studied by Maddirevula et al. (2019) carried the homozygous ABCA2 mutation c.740dupT (Gly248ArgfsTer38).
checks.evidence_quote: homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38])
checks.explanation: The variant matches the paper exactly.

checks.claim: One family studied by Maddirevula et al. (2019) carried the homozygous ABCA2 mutation c.1027C-T (Gln343Ter).
checks.explanation: This is equivalent notation for the same variant.

checks.claim: In both families studied by Maddirevula et al. (2019), the ABCA2 mutation fully segregated with the disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: two families with global developmental delay and intellectual disability (Fig. 2) that fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Aslam and Naz (2019) used whole-exome sequencing to study a consanguineous Pakistani family with 2 sibs affected by cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria. They identified a frameshift mutation in the ABCA2 gene (c.4993delG; Val1665TyrfsTer36). Sanger sequencing showed that the mutation segregated with the disorder. It was absent from all publicly available databases and from ethnically matched controls.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) used whole-exome sequencing to study a consanguineous Pakistani family with 2 sibs affected by cerebellar ataxia with dysarthria.
checks.evidence_quote: Molecular analyses included whole-exome sequencing in order to delineate the underlying pathology of the disorder.
checks.explanation: The family and phenotype are described elsewhere in the abstract.

checks.claim: Aslam and Naz (2019) identified a frameshift mutation in the ABCA2 gene, c.4993delG (Val1665TyrfsTer36), in the Pakistani family.
checks.evidence_quote: identified a frameshift variant, c.4993delG:p.(Val1665TyrfsTer36) in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2)
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

checks.claim: Sanger sequencing showed that the ABCA2 c.4993delG mutation segregated with the disorder in the Pakistani family.
checks.evidence_quote: Segregation of variants with the phenotype was checked by Sanger sequencing.
checks.explanation: The results confirm that the variant segregated with the disorder.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.4993delG mutation was absent from all publicly available databases.
checks.evidence_quote: was absent from all publicly available databases and ethnically matched controls
checks.explanation: Stated directly.

paragraphs.text: Maddirevula et al. (2019) identified a homozygous 1-bp duplication (c.740dupT, NM_212533.2) in the ABCA2 gene in a family with global developmental delay and intellectual disability. The duplication was predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (Gly248ArgfsTer38). It was found through autozygome and exome analysis and fully segregated with the disorder in the family.

checks.explanation: c.740dupT is a 1-bp duplication, and the transcript matches.

checks.evidence_quote: NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38]
checks.explanation: The protein notation in the paper means a frameshift with premature termination.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.740dupT duplication was found through autozygome and exome analysis.
checks.evidence_quote: Autozygome and exome analysis of patients with suspected Mendelian phenotypes.
checks.explanation: This is the study method used to find all variants.

checks.claim: The ABCA2 c.740dupT duplication fully segregated with the disorder in the family.
checks.evidence_quote: fully segregated with homozygous truncating variants in ABCA2 (NM_212533.2:c.740dupT:p.[Gly248Argfs*38])
checks.explanation: The paper states this directly.

paragraphs.text: Aslam and Naz (2019) identified a 1-bp deletion (c.4993delG, NM_212533.2) in the ABCA2 gene in 2 sibs from a consanguineous Pakistani family with cerebellar ataxia and dysarthria. The deletion was predicted to cause a frameshift (Val1665TyrfsTer36). It was found by whole-exome sequencing, and Sanger sequencing showed that it segregated with the disorder. The variant was absent from all publicly available databases and from ethnically matched controls.
